coverage_explanation: Exercises all eight physical sensor combinations using single-sensor transitions. Checks that the displayed occupied-layer count stays within 0..3, changes when any one sensor changes, and returns to its original value when the original inputs are restored. Sensor occupied-level polarity is unspecified, so absolute counts and the physical combination representing full occupancy cannot be asserted independently. The restock timeout, serial command syntax, record semantics, and LED behavior are also unspecified; timeout reporting, full-state buzzer/record locking, serial queries/reset, and LED behavior are therefore not independently checked.
assumptions: Each digital occupancy sensor has a stable binary interpretation: one physical level means occupied and the other means empty. No particular polarity is assumed, including across different sensors.
The TM1637 displays the current occupied-layer count as a number; leading blanks or zeros are acceptable.
Inputs are held for 1200 ms and display checks allow 900 ms settling time because no response deadline is specified.
No button or individual-LED bench defaults are needed for the tested behavior. D13 has no specified application behavior.
The empty-duration threshold, occupied input polarity, serial query/reset command grammar, new-record representation, and buzzer cadence/frequency are missing parameters.

The reference sketch makes permitted implementation choices that are not imposed on candidates: active-HIGH occupancy, a 60000 ms restock threshold, STATUS and RESET commands, a continuous 1000 Hz full alarm, and D13 indicating full occupancy.
